EFFECTIVE_MODEL: opencode/space-bunny-free | settings: none specified, none reported | runtimeMode: full-access (T3) | interactionMode: plan | evidence: requested = "independent Stage C review sub-agent, no model named"; configured/confirmed = harness label `opencode/space-bunny-free` and T3 runtime note only. Model family behind "Space Bunny Free" is UNVERIFIED — I did not enumerate the roster and no provider-side identity assertion was returned, so I make no claim of verified reviewer diversity. Full access + plan mode is NOT a hard read-only boundary; the read-only posture here is instruction-based and I complied (no repo writes; all experiments ran in `/private/var/folders/.../T/opencode/sc-review` and `tempfile` homes with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`). Baseline verified as `085e28d`; all inspection used `git diff HEAD`.

VERDICT: changes_required

BLOCKERS:

1. **`skill_lens/core/resolver.py:139-144` (`entrypoint_alias`) + `:457` (`_installation`) vs `skill_lens/core/diff.py:475`, `skill_lens/core/scanner.py:182`, `skill_lens/core/compare.py:52,72-73`, `skill_lens/core/snapshot.py:489` — sibling commands now disagree on the name of one physical copy.**
   - Problem: Stage C moved identity/lookup/installation naming onto `entrypoint_alias`, which returns `Path(p).stem` for any `.md` path. `parser._document_identity()` (`parser.py:102-105`) instead returns the *parent directory name* when the file is literally `SKILL.md`/`skill.md`. `diff`, `scan` and `compare` still key on `entry.name` (the parser rule). The two rules diverge for exactly one shape: a bare `SKILL.md` sitting directly in a root directory — a shape this stage explicitly puts in scope (`docs/validation/assessment-repairs/c/stage-c-evidence.md:26`: "A root `SKILL.md` is treated as a single-file skill with ID `SKILL`", pinned by `tests/test_stage_c_repairs.py:653`).
   - Expected behaviour: one name per physical copy across `scan`, `why`, `diff`, `compare`, `snapshot_why` and `snapshot_diff` — the invariant `labels_for_entries`'s own docstring (`discovery.py:117-130`) exists to protect after finding F-16. Which of the two naming rules wins is a Stage D identity decision, but the divergence itself must not ship: today `why` prints a name that `diff` then refuses to accept.
   - Evidence (synthetic sandbox home, no real HOME, `/etc` untouched): with `~/.gemini/config/skills/SKILL.md` present — `entry.name='skills'`; `why antigravity SKILL` → `found=True`, `installation.name='SKILL'`; `why antigravity root_skill` → `found=True`; `diff SKILL` → `found=False`; `diff skills` → `found=True`; `scan` row → `'skills'`; `snapshot_diff(...).skill_name='skills'`. Identical shape under `~/.pi/agent/skills/SKILL.md`: `why pi SKILL` → found, name `SKILL`; `why pi skills` → not found; `diff pi SKILL` → `found=False`, `diff pi skills` → `found=True`. Pre-Stage-C both commands used `entry.name`, so this divergence is new. No test catches it: `test_opencode_v2_root_md_and_nested_exact_skill_md:653` asserts the alias in isolation and never cross-checks `diff`/`scan`.

2. **`skill_lens/core/discovery.py:517-530` (the `OPENCODE_V2` branch of `_list_recursive_entries`), reached because of `discovery.py:592` — OpenCode's new recursive walk never sees symlinked skill directories below the root.**
   - Problem: `os.walk(base)` runs with the default `followlinks=False`, so a symlinked directory is never yielded as a walk root. A skill directory reached through a symlink at depth ≥ 1 is silently dropped. The *same function's* root-level branch (`discovery.py:504-513`) resolves symlinks explicitly, so the format handles symlinked skill directories at depth 0 and not below. `discovery.py:592` routes all four OpenCode roots through this walker even though their TOMLs do not set `recursive`, so this is newly exposed exposure for OpenCode, not pre-existing for it.
   - Expected behaviour: at minimum, depth-0 and deeper symlinked skill directories must be treated consistently by one entry format; the symlink-farm-shaped layouts this product exists to diagnose are exactly the case F07's acceptance names ("including symlinked files, with correct provenance").
   - Evidence: `~/.config/opencode/skills/top_link -> store/top_link` (root-level symlink) **is** discovered; `~/.config/opencode/skills/deep/deep_link -> store/deep_link` is **not**; plain `~/.config/opencode/skills/deep/plain` is. The same gap is pre-existing on already-recursive roots (`dsh_profiles` misses `linked_store/skills/plugin_skill`), so one shared walker change fixes both — but Stage C widened the blast radius to four more roots.

3. **`skill_lens/core/discovery.py:448-453` and `:470-476` (use `_is_skill_dir`) vs `:449-451`, `:471-472`, `:512`, `:527` (use `_has_exact_skill_md`) — the "exact `SKILL.md`" rule is applied to two of the four entry formats, with no evidence line for the permissive side.**
   - Problem: `DIRECTORY` and `STANDALONE_MD` roots still go through `parser.find_skill_document`, which accepts lowercase `skill.md` (`parser.py:33` `_SKILL_FILENAMES`). `QUALIFIED_STANDALONE_MD` and `OPENCODE_V2` use the new exact `os.listdir` check. The same on-disk directory therefore enters the inventory for some agents and not others purely as a function of this stage's format dispatch. `compare` groups by agent, so it will surface that implementation artifact as a capability divergence. `stage-c-evidence.md` documents only the Pi strictness (§1); the permissive directory-format rule is an undocumented discovery rule, which is the provenance gap golden rule 6 exists to prevent.
   - Expected behaviour: one exactness rule across all directory-based formats, or an explicit registry declaration plus evidence line for the difference, before `compare` reports it as a divergence. (Which side is correct is Stage D's call; the undocumented asymmetry is the C-scope defect.)
   - Evidence: one synthetic home with `<root>/lower/skill.md` (valid frontmatter) yields discovered entries for `claude`, `codex`, `dsh`, `antigravity` and **no** entry for `pi`.

SUGGESTIONS: (non-blocking)

- **Answering the specific `EntryFormat.LEGACY_FILE` question — it is not a neutral test seam.** It lives in `skill_lens/models/enums.py:101`, is accepted by `_parse_root` (so any registry TOML may declare it), and has three live branches in `_list_entries:468,478`. Its semantics are asymmetric within one declared format: a plain file is recorded `is_file=True`, a symlink to a file is recorded `is_file=False`. Reproduced — under a `legacy_file` root, `plain.md` → `is_file=True`, `linked.md` (symlink to a valid `.md` skill) → `is_file=False` with a valid parse. So the format introduced to model suffixless captures also silently reclassifies ordinary `.md` symlinks, and `resolver.py:579-580` would then report the directory `rule_id` for a symlinked `.md` on any `legacy_file` root that also carries a `file_rule_id`. It is also unnecessary: F17 is already represented under a *supported* format by `test_historical_f17_symlink_standalone_target_outside_scanned_root` (Pi `qualified_standalone_md`, the exact "symlinked standalone with correct provenance" case F07 asks for), and `test_suffixless_symlink_to_standalone_file` can keep its real subject — capturing a canonical file living outside every root — by using a `.md` symlink under `antigravity_global` (`standalone_md`) or a Pi root. Recommend dropping `LEGACY_FILE` and rewiring the two tests; if it is kept for the suffixless case, give it an explicit test-only docstring and align the symlink branch with the plain-file branch.
- `discovery.py:368-384` `_is_symlinked_markdown` now has **zero** callers after `_list_entries` was rewritten. Its careful `RuntimeError`/`OSError` handling and its comment about `file_rule_id` no longer protect anything.
- `resolver.py:183-184` `_matches` has no callers in `skill_lens/` or `tests/`; `_identity_names` (`:162-180`) is now reachable only from `_matches`. `__all__` was widened to export `entrypoint_alias`/`lookup_name_for_entry` while these two stale helpers were left behind. Given the repo's stated habit that "a test that cannot fail is worse than no test", dead discovery/resolver helpers are the same class of finding.
- `RootHit.is_file` is recorded but never used for rule selection: `resolver.py:579-580` still calls `hit.rule_for(entry.is_file)` with the merged-entry flag, while `RootHit`'s docstring (`discovery.py:163-165`) asserts "the file rule id belongs to the hit — not to the merged entry". Use `hit.is_file` or drop the claim; today the docstring overstates the model.
- `snapshot.py:142` inserts the new `registry` parameter **before** `cancelled`, so an external or TUI caller passing `cancelled` positionally would silently bind it to `registry`. No in-repo call site does this (verified), so it is latent, not live — but `*, registry=None` would remove the hazard. Related: `test_session_snapshot.py:855-862` monkeypatches `snapshot_module.load_registry` instead of using the new injection, so the parameter's intended use is only exercised at `test_session_snapshot.py:1888`.
- `_parse_root`'s `entry_format` default (`"standalone_md" if file_rule_id else "directory"`) is now unreachable for every shipped registry. It is a reasonable third-party compat shim but it *silently* changes behavior for any root without `entry_format`: standalone `.md` files that used to be discovered are now ignored. Worth a comment marking it a compatibility default rather than an evidenced one. `test_metadata_enum_validation:850-879` covers only the `DIRECTORY` default; the `file_rule_id` → `STANDALONE_MD` branch, which is the one carrying behavior, is untested.
- Test-quality gaps against the stated acceptance lines: (a) nothing asserts **default** equals **`--cwd .`** for the same project — `test_cli_cwd_live_terminal_relative` only exercises explicit `--cwd sub` / `--cwd .` with `terminal_cwd` monkeypatched; the equality holds by construction in `_effective_cwd:195-199` but the acceptance line is unasserted. (b) No test asserts a *malformed root-level* `SKILL.md` still errors under a `standalone_md`/`directory` root — only Pi's `bad_decl` directory case is covered. (c) `test_codex_plugin_readme_is_incidental_not_error` asserts discovery-level absence only; it never runs `doctor` or `--fail-on error`, which is precisely how F07 was reproduced (plan line 209). (d) On the deleted `test_resolver_nonempty_captured_overrides_disables_directory_key`: the removal is defensible — codex is `frontmatter_name` and declares no `disabled_settings`, so a directory-key override is unreachable configuration for it — and the replacement `test_synthetic_identity_source_disabled_overrides_matching` is *stronger* on identity policy (fm / dir / hybrid, positive and negative). Its weakness is that it is built entirely on synthetic `AgentDefinition`s, so the real `.claude/settings.json` → `skillOverrides` path is no longer covered at unit level (it is still covered by the `disabled_override` golden). Net acceptable, with (c) as the real gap.
- `discovery.py:255` and `:270-273`: the diff escaped docstring quotes to `\"` inside non-raw docstrings. Harmless, inconsistent with the rest of the file.
- `discovery.py:322-330`: `root.base` is silently ignored for project and absolute roots, and the `.config/` prefix is stripped by string test (`root.path.startswith(".config/")`). A registry author who sets `base = "xdg_config_home"` on a project root gets home-relative resolution with no warning; `_parse_root` could reject that combination.
- Because OpenCode's four roots are now walked to `MAX_WALK_DEPTH = 4`, any `SKILL.md` anywhere under `~/.config/opencode/skills` or `~/.agents/skills` (vendored `node_modules`, for example) enters the **global** inventory and appears in every `scan` as an UNSEARCHED row for agents that never search it. This follows the V2 evidence, but the depth/boundary rule is an unpinned implementation choice; record it in the evidence doc rather than leaving it implicit, since Stage D owns OpenCode V2.
- `discovery.py:400` calls `parse_skill()` on every `.md` child of a Pi root to decide discoverability, and `_build_entry` then parses again plus hashes — correct, but ~2× parse + 1× hash per markdown file in a Pi root. Worth a note if a root ever holds many documents.
- `_absolute_roots_allowed` is unchanged, but `test_cli_cwd_live_terminal_relative` is the first test to run live (sandbox-off) discovery; it is safe only because the autouse `isolate_system_roots` fixture in `tests/conftest.py` redirects absolute roots. That coupling is worth a comment in the new test so a future refactor does not turn it into a real `/etc/codex` probe.

FILES_AT_RISK: `skill_lens/core/resolver.py` (naming divergence, dead `_matches`/`_identity_names`, `rule_for` call site, per-hit override); `skill_lens/core/discovery.py` (format dispatch, `_has_exact_skill_md` coverage gap, `OPENCODE_V2` walker, dead `_is_symlinked_markdown`, `normalize_cwd`); `skill_lens/models/enums.py` (`EntryFormat.LEGACY_FILE`); `skill_lens/core/snapshot.py` (new `registry` kwarg position; `snapshot_why`/`snapshot_diff` naming); `skill_lens/registry/loader.py` (`_parse_root` compat defaults, new `__all__`); `skill_lens/registry/agents/{opencode,pi,codex,antigravity}.toml`; `skill_lens/cli.py` (`_effective_cwd`); `tests/test_session_snapshot.py` (rich-fixture relocation `.codex/skills` → `.gemini/config/skills`, LEGACY_FILE monkeypatching, `opaque_link` now undiscoverable and unreferenced); `tests/test_stage_c_repairs.py` (untracked); `docs/validation/assessment-repairs/c/stage-c-evidence.md` (untracked). **Extra changes: none** — `git status --porcelain` shows exactly the 14 modified files named in the brief plus the two untracked paths; `.workbuddy-ai/` and `dist/` are gitignored and untouched.

CONCEDED:

- I initially reported that `snapshot_why` loses per-hit disabled state because it derives a single `lookup_name` from the top-ranked hit. On reproduction this was a defect in my own harness: my synthetic agent declared no `disabled_settings`, so `capture_session` captured no overrides. With `disabled_settings=".g/settings.json"` set, live `why original` → DISABLED and `snapshot_why` → DISABLED, matching. Withdrawn.
- I suspected a cross-Python divergence in the rewritten symlink branch (`Path.resolve()` raising `RuntimeError` on 3.11/3.12 but stopping at a loop on 3.13+). `discovery.py:439-442` catches both, so both paths converge on `(child, False)` and there is no divergence. Withdrawn.
- I suspected `entry.is_file` OR-merging in `_merge_entries` could corrupt `entrypoint_alias` for a directory named e.g. `my.skill`; unreachable, because two entrypoints sharing a canonical target must both be files or both directories.
- I considered flagging the removal of `test_resolver_nonempty_captured_overrides_disables_directory_key` as a coverage loss. On reading codex's registry it declares no `disabled_settings`/`disabled_key`, so the configuration under test was unreachable for that agent, and the synthetic replacement covers the identity policy more completely. Not a blocker; noted under Suggestions (d).

**Scope notes carried forward for Stage D (not C blockers):** OpenCode V2 recursive depth/boundary and plugin rules; the choice between the two naming rules in Blocker 1; which directory formats should require exact `SKILL.md`; Pi lowercase-`skill.md` and OpenCode symlink behaviour need vendor evidence before the rule is pinned. **A/B guarantees:** the frozen-capture stability check (`snapshot.py:346`) still includes `entry.is_file`, XDG isolation verified end-to-end (external `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` under a sandbox falls back to `<sandbox>/.config` with zero escape; both in-sandbox copies discovered; unset XDG behaves identically), and the four coordinator gates plus four mutations are accepted as gate evidence only, not as correctness conclusions. No claim is made about the A–H campaign beyond Stage C.
